points: Terminators mark start/end; rectangles perform processes; parallelograms represent input/output.
Decision diamonds choose labeled alternatives. Arrows specify order and loop-back paths.
Test both branches and boundary inputs before accepting a chart.
lesson.example: Start → Read n → n > 0? → Yes/No output → End
lesson.title: Flowcharting

controls.summary: Drag flowchart symbols onto numbered positions and follow the arrows. Check chart executes every case. Arrow keys and Enter also place selected blocks.

objective: Read value for station 2, then display the same value without changing it. Problem values 15, 5; test inputs [{'value': -15}, {'value': 0}, {'value': 15}].
title: Flowchart Lab · Input and output
subtitle: Mt. Pyre – Crater Lake Edge: the edge of a glowing crater
win_condition: Build and check a chart that produces the required outputs for every example input.
lose_condition: The run ends after the available unsuccessful chart checks are used.
hint: Trace the arrows. Read input before using it; use rectangles for assignments and diamonds for decisions.
